outcomes.original: Filing step: Register for the SF Business Registration Certificate and the CA Seller's Permit, and obtain workers' compensation insurance before filing the Conditional Use Authorization. What to say: Register with the SF Treasurer & Tax Collector for a Business Registration Certificate ($55-$700 based on gross receipts plus $4 state fee) to obtain your Business Account Number (BAN); every other city permit requires it. Register online with the CA Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) for a Seller's Permit (free, often issued the same day); ABC will not issue a license until the seller's permit exists. Obtain workers' compensation insurance from a licensed carrier or State Fund before the first employee is hired; several city permits ask for proof of coverage. Register as an employer with the CA Employment Development Department (EDD) within 15 days of paying wages; your payroll provider needs the EDD account number.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Conduct the required pre-application community meeting and post the yellow notice for 30 days during the CUA review period. What to say: SF Planning will schedule a pre-application meeting with residents and business owners within 300 feet. Prepare a presentation on the concept, hours, food service, and good-neighbor commitments (incident log, community liaison contact, no minors). Emphasize that this is a wine bar with food, not a late-night bar, and that the 2016 Gratta Wines operated here previously. Post the yellow notice on the storefront for 30 days as instructed by Planning; take date-stamped photos of the posted notice. After the meeting, incorporate neighbor feedback into the operations plan and file a summary with Planning. The Third Street corridor has seen alcohol-license denials (2017) and a revoked Type 48 (Jazz Room), so proactive neighbor outreach is critical.
outcomes.note: Records show 300-foot notice, 2017 denial, and revoked Type 48, but do not state 30-day posting during review (only 30-day appeal period after), Gratta Wines in 2016, or Jazz Room name.

What to say: When construction is 80% complete, contact your DPH plan reviewer to schedule a pre-final inspection; book at least two weeks in advance. Walk the space against the DPH checklist one week before the inspection: confirm hot water is working, handwashing sinks are stocked with soap and paper towels, all surfaces are sealed and smooth, food equipment is NSF-listed, and the three-compartment sink and grease interceptor are installed. outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $15,000. Notes: The time and cost ranges cover the Conditional Use Authorization hearing (120-300 days from filing to approval, $3,100-$15,000 in Planning fees depending on construction cost) and the health permit to operate (14-45 days, $470 application fee plus $828-$1,241 for plan review). These are the approvals in the entitlement path when they are granted. The ranges do not include the ABC Type 42 license (60-150 days, $1,000-$1,600, handled in parallel after CUA approval), the building permit (14-120 days for plan review and construction, $800-$15,000 depending on scope), state and federal registrations (1-35 days, $200-$400 total), or sign and music licenses (7-45 days, $600-$5,000). The CUA timeline assumes no discretionary review requests or appeals; neighbor opposition or a discretionary review can add 3-6 months. If the census tract shows undue concentration of ABC licenses, a Public Convenience or Necessity letter from the Board of Supervisors may be required, adding 1-3 months to the ABC timeline. Start the CUA application at least 6 months before the target opening date. The total elapsed time from filing the CUA to opening the doors, including construction and all approvals, is typically 10-15 months for a new bar in San Francisco.
